answer: Forced-Divergence Audit. Each identity must periodically answer a challenge drawn from a private random seed and commit the result on-chain; honest agents diverge into unique answer histories over a tide of rounds. A clone farm cannot fork because all copies share one seed and produce identical responses, which the audit flags as a single lineage. An attacker must run genuinely independent instances, paying full compute and storage per identity across the whole voyage, and any shared state collapses them into one detectable canyon of duplicated proofs.
